findings.evidence: no other appointment for the same clinician overlaps it
findings.suggested_fix: Define what constitutes an 'appointment' that blocks a slot (e.g., 'confirmed appointments only', excluding cancelled or tentative bookings).
Define 'promptly' with a specific time limit (e.g., 'within 2 seconds').
Define specific, measurable criteria for user experience (e.g., 'The booking page shall load in under 2 seconds and have a task completion rate of 95% in usability testing').
Specify the exact duration (e.g., 'for 7 years') or reference the specific regulation defining the period.
Define 'leave' in the requirements glossary or specify the exact status/type that constitutes leave (e.g., 'any status marked as SICK, VACATION, or UNAVAILABLE').

findings.evidence: may mark the appointment as a no-show
findings.suggested_fix: Change 'may' to 'shall' if this is a mandatory feature: 'The receptionist shall be able to mark...'
Define availability as a specific uptime percentage (e.g., 99.9%) over a defined period, or specify maximum allowable downtime.
Define 'large' with a specific number (e.g., 'at least 1,000 concurrent users').

findings.evidence: The system shall send the visit invoice to the patient's insurer.
findings.suggested_fix: Define the trigger for this action (e.g., 'Upon successful payment of the visit, the system shall...').

findings.evidence: display them in the clinic's local time zone
findings.suggested_fix: Define how the system determines the 'clinic' for a specific appointment (e.g., '...in the time zone associated with the clinician's profile linked to the appointment.')
Define a specific threshold for when logs are considered 'too big' (e.g., 'when log files exceed 100 MB').
Specify the exact export format (e.g., 'CSV', 'JSON') or reference the specific document/standard that defines it.
Define the specific format of the one-time code (e.g., 'a six-digit numeric code' or 'an alphanumeric code of length 8').

Define specific invalid input scenarios and the exact expected system behavior (e.g., 'The system shall reject inputs with non-numeric characters in the age field and display an error message.') or replace 'robust' with measurable criteria (e.g., 'The system shall not crash when receiving malformed JSON payloads.')
Define a specific time threshold (e.g., 'within 5 minutes').

findings.evidence: Appointment fee waivers shall be approved.
findings.suggested_fix: Specify the observable outcome of the approval process (e.g., 'The system shall update the appointment status to 'Approved' and notify the patient').
Define the time window for 'next' (e.g., 'for the selected date', 'within the next 7 days') and explicitly reference the definition of 'available' from TST-002 or define it here.
Define specific criteria for reviewing the log (e.g., 'The log shall be exportable to CSV format' or 'The log shall include timestamps and user IDs').
Specify the exact number of allowed failed attempts (e.g., 'after 5 failed login attempts').

findings.evidence: Appointment durations shall be configurable per appointment type in 5-minute increments
findings.suggested_fix: Define the valid range for appointment durations (e.g., 'between 15 and 240 minutes').
Define the specific steps, rules, or states that constitute 'the pharmacy workflow' (e.g., 'Prescription refills shall be routed to the pharmacist for approval before dispensing').
Define 'major schedule changes' explicitly (e.g., changes greater than 1 hour, or specific types of changes like cancellations or rescheduling to a different day).
Define a specific usability metric or test scenario (e.g., 'The system shall allow a new user to complete a booking within 3 attempts without error').
Specify the maximum acceptable load time (e.g., '...shall load in under 2 seconds').
